author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human: workspace-wide /set parameter-shape decision.

The bead frames two related divergences:

1. create: Option<HashMap<String, FooType>> (calendars, typed) vs Option<serde_json::Value> (canonical mail-client, untyped)
2. destroy: Option<&[Id]> (calendars, borrowed slice) vs Option<Vec<Id>> (canonical mail-client, owned Vec)

This is parallel to bd:JMAP-1j9k.14 (destroy slice vs Vec only) and bd:JMAP-1j9k.13 (workspace-wide /copy args sweep) and bd:JMAP-1j9k.2 (filter API shape). All four are workspace-architectural decisions that affect the canonical mail-client AND all 5 other extension-client siblings.

The bead author offers:
- Option A: calendars matches canonical (untyped create + owned destroy). Calendars-only mechanical change.
- Option B: canonical changes first, sweep all siblings.

Per workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template rule, the divergent state right now (calendars-only typed/borrowed) IS the regression. Choose a path before 0.x.y ships.

My recommendation if forced: option A. The canonical is canonical; brings calendars into alignment with the workspace's stated authoritative template. The wire-correctness gap that motivated typed-create in calendars (JMAP-1j9k.1) was fixable in the types crate (making Calendar.id Option<Id>, which we just did), so the typed-create no longer carries a defect the untyped form can't match.

Also: cross-link to bd:JMAP-ip5u (sweep for if_in_state arg, decision already-taken). The same family of workspace-wide /set shape decisions can be tracked under a single workspace-design epic. Worth filing one once the human picks a direction.

Skipping in /do-beads loop.
